reviewed_sources.title: Motional Casimir force
reviewed_sources.authors: Marc Thierry Jaekel and Serge Reynaud
reviewed_sources.edition: Journal de Physique I 2 (1992), 149-165; arXiv quant-ph/0101069v1
reviewed_sources.read_scope: Scoped rereading: introduction, Gaussian force-noise contractions equations (15)-(17), and linear-response Hamiltonian/susceptibility equations (18)-(19). This does not claim a new complete reading of its scattering algebra, appendix A or cited proof dependencies.
reviewed_sources.comparison: Gaussian pressure pair spectra and their motional linear response are established. This note derives its graph-specific uniform boundary-capacity and fixed-band estimates directly; the mirror formulas do not prove the charged-graph ultraviolet completion.

reused_dependencies: The canonical energy-space contraction and two-frequency rank comparison, moving-mouth Ward vertex, proper-cut kinematics and prescribed free contact completion retain their earlier source/proof scopes. No new full literature exit is claimed.
unused_leads: Searches also returned mathematical spectral papers, graph Casimir examples and unrelated wormhole models. Snippets are discovery leads only; none are used to establish the uniform theorem or priority.
The second Jaekel-Reynaud PDF, quant-ph/0101068, was reopened but no additional proof claim rests on that access.
access_notes: The unversioned arXiv PDF identifies v1; the downloaded exact bytes are hashed. The first two searches were submitted before context compaction and their output was not retained in the visible reading; no source review is claimed from those results.
The central literature register has incoming changes and is preserved unchanged.
development_notes: The initial dense generalized eigensolver run passed the first mesh family and the first two meshes of the second family, then failed the unchanged 2e-7 Green-identity tolerance with normalized error 4.2332249e-7 at epsilon=1e-4 and 128 half-cells. Its source is retained in references/cache/pressure-band-initial-check.py.

A shift-invert generalized eigensolver now targets the low spectrum directly instead of using an absolute eigenvalue tolerance affected by the very high graded-mesh eigenvalues. All accuracy and refinement thresholds are retained. The final receipt records the terminal outcome and exact source.

That corrected solver passed the Green checks but the epsilon=1e-4 scalar eigenfrequency missed the fixed 3e-4 accuracy threshold at 128 half-cells: errors at 32,64,128 were 0.0050405205, 0.0012884437, 0.0003238773, showing second-order convergence. The final mesh family for that case is 64,128,256, with the same absolute and convergence thresholds. The intermediate source is retained in references/cache/pressure-band-shift-invert-check.py.
The independent negative-energy ODE uses an explicitly real squared spectral parameter, removing a harmless complex-to-real warning for k=i.
No fitted sample constant supplies the uniform bound; analytic capacity, form duality, Bessel and positive pair-measure estimates do.
novelty_assessment: Continue physical long-return damping as provisional primary and matched finite-duration transfer as fallback. Charged boundary capacity and positive Dirichlet-to-Neumann estimates control the actual pressure vertex in every fixed frequency band, including soft modes and unequal returns. The filtered proper-interacting versus canonical-free correction divided by q delta is O(log^4(q)/sqrt(q)+log^10(q)/q) in the retained scaling. Renormalized ultraviolet response, mass-dependent contacts and physical geometry/state/exterior remain unresolved; physical damping and consequential novelty are not accepted.
